# src/vendor/host/ - reserved, and deliberately empty

This directory exists because `dsh-as-aistudio` has one and the studio's
architecture is copied from it. Nothing is vendored into it here, and that is a
decision, not an omission.

`dsh-as-aistudio` copies each component's HOST half into this directory and mounts
the copy. That makes the studio installable with no component packages present at
all - but it also means a component's fix reaches the studio only through a
re-vendor and a studio release, and, worse, that uninstalling a component changes
nothing: the row still starts, `/status` still reports it mounted, and its buttons
keep appearing with no code behind them.

This studio inverts that (docs/INTEROP.md section 11): `src/shell.js` imports the
real component package, so

* the host logic exists exactly once - the copy the component's release ships;
* a missing component fails its own row, `/status` reports `hostMounted: false`
  with the reason, and the browser half mounts nothing for it;
* a component's fix reaches the studio by upgrading the component, not by
  re-releasing the studio.

Only the BROWSER halves are vendored (`src/vendor/<component>.js`), because a
bundle is served per Loader row and there is no way to delegate that. They are
generated by `tools/vendor.mjs` and must never be edited by hand.

Nothing in this package reads this directory. It is published (see the `files`
array in package.json) only so that the layout stays self-explanatory.
